title: A magazine in the laundromat
situation: You are {{Kara}}. While {{Alice}} warms up by the dryers, there is a magazine on the cupboard by the laundromat door.

media.title: Century: The Bee-Line to Disaster
facts: Wild bees have been declared extinct; one in three mouthfuls of food depends on pollination and famine is expected, so {{CyberLife}} is building robotic bees.

media.title: Gossips Weekly: Face the Music
facts: Young people only attend virtual concerts; a campaign is trying to bring live music back.

adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

title: The laundromat
situation: You are {{Kara}}. You and {{Alice}} are on the street in the rain with nothing, and androids are easy to spot in uniform. In a laundromat a man is asleep next to a dryer full of his clothes. You could take a change of clothes, cut off the marker on your uniform, and pass for human. {{Alice}} quietly says that stealing is wrong.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} changes into the stolen clothes, cuts the marker from her temple and tells {{Alice}} it was necessary. They could pass for human now.
outcomes.1: They leave the laundromat as they came in, {{Kara}} still in her android uniform.

title: The convenience store
situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is getting dark and cold. {{Alice}} is shivering and you have no money for a room. In a convenience store the clerk shrugs when you ask for help. The register is open whenever he turns away. {{Alice}} could knock over a display to distract him while you take the cash. If you have {{Todd}}'s gun you could simply point it at him.

options.text: Have {{Alice}} distract the clerk and take money from the register.
Threaten the clerk with the gun and demand money.

adaptationNote: Option 1 requires the gun from Stormy Night.

outcomes.0: {{Alice}} knocks over a display, the clerk turns, and {{Kara}} empties the register into her pocket. They walk out with enough for a room.
outcomes.1: The clerk freezes with his hands up and {{Kara}} takes the money from the till. They walk out with enough for a room.
outcomes.2: They leave the store with nothing.

title: Where to sleep
situation: You are {{Kara}}. Night has fallen and it is pouring. The options you can see: a cheap motel across the street, which takes cash and will only rent to someone who looks human; an abandoned, boarded-up house at the end of the lot; or a wrecked car in the parking lot you could shelter in for the night.

options.text: Pay for a room at the motel.
Spend the night in the abandoned car.

adaptationNote: The motel requires both money and the clothing disguise.

outcomes.0: The night clerk barely looks up. {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} get a warm room with a bed and a shower, and {{Alice}} falls asleep almost at once.
outcomes.1: {{Kara}} forces a way into the boarded-up house. It is cold and filthy, but it is out of the rain.
outcomes.2: They climb into the wrecked car and {{Kara}} holds {{Alice}} through a freezing, sleepless night.

title: The motel television
situation: You are {{Kara}}. The motel room television is on when you come in. {{Alice}} is already curling up on the bed.

media.title: the local news
facts: {{CyberLife}} opened the city's first android zoo, recreating hundreds of extinct species across a hundred acres.

adaptationNote: Optional reading or viewing. Contents are summarized from the in-game magazine articles and broadcasts. Watching certain news reports about android incidents lowers public opinion, as in the game.

title: {{Ralph}}
situation: You are {{Kara}}. The abandoned house is not empty. An android named {{Ralph}}, his face badly scarred by humans, is squatting here; he is twitchy, talks to himself, and keeps a knife. He offers you and {{Alice}} shelter and, later, a dead rodent he caught for her dinner. He is unpredictable but he has not threatened you.

options.text: Accept his hospitality and treat him kindly.
Stay polite but keep {{Alice}} away from him and refuse his food.
Pull the gun on him so he knows not to come near {{Alice}}.

adaptationNote: Threatening {{Ralph}} makes him betray you to the police later and removes him from the camp. Option 2 requires the gun.

outcomes.0: {{Ralph}} is delighted. He gives {{Alice}} the best spot by the fire and talks to her, badly, about rabbits.
outcomes.1: {{Ralph}} shrugs and talks to himself. {{Alice}} stays close to {{Kara}} all night.
outcomes.2: {{Ralph}} shrinks back from the gun, muttering that he meant no harm, and keeps his distance for the rest of the night.

title: {{Alice}}'s question
situation: You are {{Kara}}. Settling {{Alice}} down for the night, you tell her about going somewhere safe, maybe across the border. She asks whether you will always stay together. You have no idea what tomorrow brings and you are being hunted.

options.text: Promise her you will always be together.
Tell her honestly that you cannot promise that.

outcomes.0: {{Alice}} smiles for the first time and holds on to her. {{Kara}} tells her about going somewhere safe across the river.
outcomes.1: {{Alice}} goes quiet and turns away. {{Kara}} tells her about going somewhere safe across the river.
